subject: AcreetionOS Update — June 21, 2026
body:
Our continuous integration pipeline has just seen another round of fine-tuning, with the recent introduction of per-pipeline staging directories and relative symlinks for the latest ISO images significantly boosting the reliability and efficiency of our release process. This change is now reflected in our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html, where you can find detailed information about the latest developments in our project.

Development
The development team has been hard at work, with recent commits including the use of relative symlinks for latest.iso and per-pipeline staging directories to avoid publish races between concurrent builds, all of which can be found in our code repository. We're also keeping up with the latest software releases, including the recent Emacs 31.1 release, which brings a long list of changes and improvements. For more information on how to get the most out of Emacs on AcreetionOS, be sure to check out our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html.

Community
Our community has been active as always, with discussions around the latest security updates and stable kernel sets. We've also seen some interesting commits from community members, including initial releases of configs and field notes from a DL380 G7 running Arch. If you're interested in learning more about how to get involved with the AcreetionOS community, be sure to check out our wiki at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html. And for the latest news and updates, you can always visit our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html.
